content: Nystatin is a medication used to treat fungal infections, particularly those affecting the skin or mucous membranes. It is available in various forms, including oral suspension, tablets, and topical powder. Below is a detailed explanation of its uses, administration, precautions, and potential side effects: Oral Suspension The oral suspension is typically prescribed at a dosage of 400,000 to 600,000 units to be taken by mouth every six hours. Oral Tablets Nystatin tablets are usually prescribed at a dosage of 500,000 to 1,000,000 units every eight hours. These are used for systemic or localized fungal infections. Powder Form The powder form is mixed in water (1/8 to 1/4 teaspoon in 1/2 cup of water, equating to 500,000 to 1,000,000 units) and taken orally every eight hours. This form is often used for specific fungal infections requiring oral administration. Liposomal Nystatin This formulation is used for the treatment of invasive fungal infections. Patients are advised to retain the suspension in the mouth for as long as possible before swallowing to maximize its antifungal effects. Topical Use Nystatin powder is applied directly to the skin to treat fungal skin infections. The affected area should be cleaned and thoroughly dried before application. The powder should be applied in a thin layer to cover the infected area and some surrounding skin. It is typically used two to three times daily, as directed by a healthcare provider. Mechanism of Action Nystatin works by binding to sterols in the fungal cell membrane, altering its permeability. This causes the contents of the fungal cell to leak out, leading to cell death. It is poorly absorbed when taken orally, and its effects are localized to the site of application. Onset and Excretion Relief of symptoms for oral candidiasis typically occurs within 24 to 72 hours. The drug is excreted unchanged in the feces. Precautions Before using nystatin, inform your doctor if you are allergic to it or have any other allergies. The product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. During pregnancy, nystatin should only be used when clearly needed. It is unknown if the drug passes into breast milk, so caution is advised for breastfeeding mothers. Nystatin is not suitable for systemic fungal infections and should not be used in such cases. Drug Interactions Nystatin may reduce the effectiveness of certain probiotics, such as Saccharomyces boulardii. It may also interact with other medications, such as voclosporin, potentially increasing the risk of nephrotoxicity or ototoxicity. Patients should inform their healthcare provider of all medications and supplements they are taking to avoid harmful interactions. Side Effects Common side effects include skin irritation, redness, diarrhea, nausea, stomach pain, and vomiting. Rare but serious side effects include Stevens-Johnson syndrome, hypersensitivity reactions, and contact dermatitis. If irritation or sensitization occurs during use, discontinue the medication and consult a healthcare provider. Overdose If nystatin is accidentally swallowed in large amounts, it may be harmful. In cases of overdose with serious symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call emergency services immediately (911 in the U.S.). Otherwise, contact a poison control center for guidance. Missed Dose If a dose is missed, take it as soon as you remember. If it is close to the time of the next dose, skip the missed dose and resume the regular schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Storage Store nystatin at room temperature. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard expired or unused medication. Important Notes This medication has been prescribed for your current condition only. Do not use it for other infections unless directed by your doctor. Always follow your healthcare provider’s instructions for the correct use of this medication. If you have any questions or concerns, consult your doctor or pharmacist for further guidance. Nystatin is a safe and effective treatment for fungal infections when used as directed.
